  columns: (1fr, auto, auto),   inset: 10pt,

  table.header(  [*Item*], [*Quantity*], [*Status*]  ),
  [Premium Widgets], [250], [In Stock],
  [Super Gadgets], [12], [Low Stock],
  [Mystery Boxes], [0], [Out of Stock]
)

## R

### GT Table - R

```{r}
#| label: tbl-gt-example
#| tbl-cap: "Table generated via gt package"
#| echo: false
library(gt)
library(tibble)

tribble(  ~Fruit, ~Price,  "Apple", 2.05,  "Pear",  1.37) |> gt()

```
gt (Great Tables): Highly recommended. Posit heavily optimized gt so that its CSS-based styles, complex multi-tier headers, and footers automatically translate into native Typst code with zero layout degradation

## typstable in R

 A specialized CRAN package built exclusively to output Typst markup. It features a pipe-friendly (|>) syntax specifically built for grouped headers, row groups, and conditional cell formatting compiled directly for Typst engines.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-typstable-demo
#| tbl-cap: "Advanced dataset formatting compiled cleanly with typstable."
#| echo: false
#| message: false

# Make sure you have installed the package first:
# install.packages("typstable")

library(typstable)
library(dplyr)

# Prepare a subset of mock performance data 
df <- tibble(  Model = c("Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma", "Delta"),
  Category = c("Core", "Core", "Edge", "Edge"),  Speed = c(95, 88, 72, 64),
  Efficiency = c(91, 84, 95, 78),  Cost = c(120, 110, 85, 75))

# Build the table using native typstable pipelines
df |>  select(Model, Category, Speed, Efficiency, Cost) |> tt( align = c("l", "c", "c", "c", "r","r"), col_names = c("Ser", "Model", "Category", "Speed (GHz)", "Efficiency (%)", "Cost (Rs)") ) |>   tt_header_above(c(" " = 3, "Performance Metrics" = 2, "Financials" = 1)) 
  
```

Refer to @tbl-typstable-demo to see how the row blocks and grouped metrics line up natively.


## tinytable in R
https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/tinytable/vignettes/tinytable_tutorial_typst.pdf

•  An excellent, lightweight alternative that features dedicated Typst engine support without drawing heavy dependencies.
The tinytable package is a newer, ultra-lightweight, and zero-dependency alternative to gt or kableExtra that works exceptionally well with Quarto and Typst. It has a clean, explicit syntax (style_tt(), format_tt(), group_tt()) and outputs clean native

```{r}
#| label: tbl-tiny-demo
#| tbl-cap: "An example table built using the tinytable engine."
#| cache: false
#| echo: false
#| message: false

# Make sure you have installed the package first:
# install.packages("tinytable")

library(tinytable)
library(dplyr)

# Create a clean mock dataset
x= mtcars

# Render and style the table
cap <- ' Tiny Table Eg'; not <- ' This is note '
tt(x, caption = cap, notes = not)  |>  style_tt(  i = 1:3,   j = 1:3,   background = "teal",   color = "white",   bold = TRUE) |> group_tt(j = list("Halloumi" = 1:2, "Tofu" = 4:5))
```

## Grouped Tables - 2

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| cache: false

library(tinytable)

tmp <- mtcars %>%  tibble::rownames_to_column("Car") %>%  arrange(gear, mpg) %>%  group_by(gear) %>%  mutate(gearGroup = paste0("Gear: ", gear, " | No. of Cars: ", n())) %>%  ungroup()
#tmp
# Group labels and last row position of each group
grp <- tmp %>%  count(gearGroup, name = "n") %>%  mutate(end = cumsum(n))
#grp
group_labels <- as.list(setNames(grp$end, grp$gearGroup))

# Create table
tt(tmp) %>%  group_tt(i = group_labels) %>%  subset(select = -gearGroup) %>%  style_tt(align = "c") %>%  style_tt(i = "groupi", align = "l",  color = "teal", line = "b") %>%  theme_typst()

```

```{=typst}
#show figure.caption: set text(
  fill: rgb("#8c2146"),
  size: 10pt,
  weight: "bold",)
```

## Grouped Tables - 3

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: tbl-gear-summary1
#| tbl-cap: "Gear Wise Summary of Cars with Average MPG and Weight and Count2"
#| cache: false
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

library(tinytable)
library(dplyr)

tmp <- mtcars %>%  tibble::rownames_to_column("Car") %>%  arrange(gear, mpg)

# Group summary
grp <- tmp %>%  group_by(gear) %>%  summarise( n = n(), avgMPG = round(mean(mpg), 2),  avgWT = round(mean(wt), 2),  .groups = "drop"  ) %>%  mutate(    label = paste0( "Gear: ", gear,  " | Cars: ", n,  " | Avg MPG: ", avgMPG,  " | Avg WT: ", avgWT   ),  end = cumsum(n)  )

group_labels <- as.list(setNames(grp$end - grp$n, grp$label))
# Generate tinytable
tt(tmp %>% select(Car, gear, mpg, wt, everything()), notes=NULL)  %>%   group_tt(i = group_labels) %>%  style_tt(align = "c") %>%  style_tt(    i = "groupi",    align = "l",    color = "teal",    line = "b"  ) %>%  theme_typst()

```

```{=typst}
#text(size: 8pt, style: "italic")[  Note: MPG = Miles per Gallon; WT = Weight in 1,000 lbs.]
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: tbl-column-widths
#| tbl-cap: "Setting Table Column Widths in TinyTable in 3 Table : Individual Captions do not work2"
#| cache: false
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

library(tinytable)
library(dplyr)

tmp <- mtcars %>%  tibble::rownames_to_column("Car") %>%  arrange(gear, mpg)
c1="T1: Setting Table Column Widths in TinyTable2"
tt(  tmp %>% head() %>% select(Car, gear, mpg, wt, everything()),  width = c(120, 45, 50, 50, rep(45, ncol(tmp) - 4)), caption = c1) %>%
  theme_typst()
c2="T2: Fractions of Table Width"
tt( tmp %>% head() %>% select(Car, gear, mpg, wt, everything()),   width = c(3, 1, 1, 1, rep(.8, ncol(tmp) - 4)), caption = c2) %>%
  theme_typst()
c3="T3: Same Width"
tt( tmp %>% head() %>% select(-Car) %>% select(gear, mpg, wt, everything()),   width = 1, caption = c3) %>%
  theme_typst()

```


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: tbl-table-options3
#| tbl-cap: "Background Color and Font Style in TinyTable3"
#| cache: false
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

pacman::p_load(tinytable, dplyr)

tt(mtcars %>% head()) %>%  style_tt(background = "#EAF4F4") %>%  theme_typst()

tt(mtcars %>% head()) %>%  style_tt(i = 0, background = "#006D77", color = "white", bold = TRUE) %>%  style_tt(i = 1:6, background = "#F0F8FF") %>%  theme_typst()

tt(mtcars %>% head()) %>%  style_tt(i = c(2, 4), background = "#FFF2CC") %>%  style_tt(j = 1, background = "#D9EAF7") %>%  theme_typst()

tt(mtcars %>% head()) %>%   style_tt(    i = seq(2, nrow(mtcars), 2),    background = "#F2F2F2"  ) %>%  theme_typst()
```
In tinytable, the background argument sets the cell fill colour, while color sets the text colour.
For your Quarto–Typst reports, it is recommended to use a dark header, light blue group headings, and a white or light-grey table body.

## Multi Column Table Report

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: tbl-table-options4
#| tbl-cap: "Background Color and Font Style in TinyTable 2"
#| cache: false
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

pacman::p_load(tinytable, dplyr, tidyr)
df <- mtcars %>%   tibble::rownames_to_column("Car") %>%  select(Car, mpg, wt)

nblock <- 3
nrows <- ceiling(nrow(df) / nblock)

df_wide <- df %>%  mutate(    block = ceiling(row_number() / nrows),    row = (row_number() - 1) %% nrows + 1
  ) %>%  pivot_wider(    id_cols = row,    names_from = block,    values_from = c(Car, mpg, wt),
    names_glue = "{.value}_{block}"  ) %>%  select(    row,    Car_1, mpg_1, wt_1,    Car_2, mpg_2, wt_2,    Car_3, mpg_3, wt_3
  ) %>%  select(-row)

tt(  df_wide,  caption = "Motor Cars: Three Side-by-Side Blocks",  width = rep(1, ncol(df_wide))) %>%  style_tt(align = "c") %>%  theme_typst()
```

```{=typst}
#pagebreak()
```

## Another Way of Multiple Column Table Report
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
library(dplyr)

iris3 <- iris %>%  mutate(ser = row_number()) %>%  select(ser, Species, Sepal.Length, Petal.Length)

# Convert each row into Typst table cells
cells <- apply(iris3, 1, function(x) {
  paste0("[", x, "]", collapse = ", ")})

typst_code <- paste0(  "#columns(3, gutter: 10pt)[\n",
  "#set text(size: 8pt)\n",
  "#table(\n",
  "columns: (0.6fr, 1.5fr, 1fr, 1fr),\n",
  "inset: 3pt,\n",
  "stroke: 0.3pt + gray.lighten(60%),\n",
  "table.header([*Ser*], [*Species*], [*Sepal*], [*Petal*]),\n",
  paste(cells, collapse = ",\n"),
  "\n)\n",
  "]")

cat("```{=typst}\n", typst_code, "\n```\n", sep = "")

```



## Long Tables (Spanning Pages)

By default, Typst wraps tables inside non-breakable figures, which prevents them from splitting across multiple pages. If you have a long table, add this show rule somewhere in your document to allow them to break gracefully across pages

`#show figure: set block(breakable: true)`{=typst}

or

```{=typst}
// Crucial: This rule allows figures (including tables) to break across page boundaries
#show figure: set block(breakable: true)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-iris-long
#| tbl-cap: "The full Iris dataset displayed across multiple pages with repeating headers."
#| echo: false
#| message: false

library(gt)

# Convert the full iris dataset into a gt table
iris |> head(40) |>  gt() |>   tab_header(    title = "Iris Dataset Measurements",    subtitle = "All 150 observations"  ) |>     opt_table_font( font = list(      google_font(name = "Roboto"),      "Arial",      "Helvetica"    ))
# # Ensures the header row repeats automatically on every new page
```

As we can see in @tbl-iris-long, the data spreads over several pages cleanly.

1. #show figure: set block(breakable: true): This is the native Typst rule that permits the table container to split across pages.
2. Native gt Translation: When format: typst is active, gt compiles the data into a native Typst #table(). Native Typst tables duplicate their table.header() onto every new page by default without needing extra R code configurations.
